color.description: channel colour(s), pipe-separated per channel, e.g. 'lime' or 'cyan|magenta' (default lime)

dry_run.description: print the ffmpeg commands that would run, run nothing

fast.description: preview quality: x264 preset veryfast (overrides --preset) for quick iterations

height.description: output height in px, must be even (default 1080)

hw.description: encode on the GPU with Apple VideoToolbox (h264/hevc/prores; Apple Silicon only): several times faster, larger files at the same quality; falls back to the CPU encoder, reported, where it cannot apply

image.description: still image or brand plate to put behind the visualisation (a local file; scaled to cover the frame and centre-cropped)

image_fit.description: how a still of the wrong aspect fills the frame: cover (default, crop the overflow), contain (bars in --background), blur (bars are a blurred copy, as fit.py)

json.description: print a JSON result (output, probe, commands) on stdout instead of the path

json_brief.description: like --json but trimmed: status, output, dry_run, verified, a compact summary of the output probe, this tool's own keys, and the command count instead of the command lines (failures print the full failure document, unchanged)

no_hw.description: encode on the CPU (x264/x265/SVT-AV1/prores_ks) even when $FFMPEG_SKILL_HW=1

on_silent.description: input audio whose peak is at or below --silence-threshold (the render would be a flat line): warn (default: render it, report `silent: true`) or fail (refuse before ffmpeg runs)

overwrite.description: allow replacing an existing output (refused without it)

plan.description: write the dry run as a plan (inputs fingerprinted, commands, expected output, verify steps) that render.py FILE executes later; implies --dry-run

platform.description: take the frame size and fps from this destination instead of --width/--height/--fps

position.description: where the visualisation sits over the plate (default strip: a band of --vis-height along the bottom, the podcast-audiogram convention)

progress.description: show percent / ETA on stderr while ffmpeg encodes

quality.description: encoder quality on the CRF scale (default 18; lower = better; 18 visually lossless for x264/x265, up to 63 for av1); ignored by prores

silence_threshold.description: peak level in dBFS at or below which the input counts as silent (default -50)

split_channels.description: draw each channel in its own lane instead of summing to one

srt.description: burn these captions into the render afterwards, by running caption.py (never re-implemented here)

text.description: plain cue file to burn, same as caption.py --text

timeout.description: kill an ffmpeg run past this many seconds, kind=timeout (default 1800; 0 = no limit)

title.description: one static label drawn over the plate, through graphics.py's sticker template

vis_height.description: height of the visualisation band as a fraction of the frame (default 0.35)

waveform_mode.description: --style waveform only: how each sample is drawn (default line)

width.description: output width in px, must be even (default 1920)

audiogram.description: {style, background ('image' or 'color'), image, position, vis_height, platform, captions, title, stages, verified} -- present on every run, so a plain waveform answers background 'color' (1.16)

commands.description: every ffmpeg command line planned or run

encoder.description: the video encoder the last ffmpeg command used (after any GPU->CPU fallback; under --dry-run the planned one; render.py and waveform.py: their stages' commands included), `copy` for a stream copy; absent when no command encoded video

hw.description: present when VideoToolbox was asked for (--hw, $FFMPEG_SKILL_HW, a render.py stage, a batch.py item), on export.py when $FFMPEG_SKILL_HW=1 is set but its delivery preset does not take it, and when this ffmpeg build has no libx264/libx265 and an encode ran on VideoToolbox instead: {requested: whether this run's encodes were asked onto VideoToolbox (false for that export, and for the build without libx264/libx265), source: flag|env|auto (auto: nobody asked, the build has no libx264/libx265 and this Apple Silicon machine ran VideoToolbox in its place), used: true|false whether the encoder that ran last is VideoToolbox, null under --dry-run (nothing ran) and when this process ran no encode itself (batch.py: its stages are child processes; its top-level hw gathers the items' requested/source/fallback/notes and each results row carries its item's encoder and hw), fallback: a job VideoToolbox refused (encoder open or compression session failure; nothing else is retried) was re-encoded on the CPU, notes: why an encode stayed on or fell back to the CPU, and, when $FFMPEG_SKILL_HW chose the GPU and it ran, what that costs and that --no-hw opts out}. A VideoToolbox encode also adds a top-level notes line: its quality is not CRF-equivalent. A kind: ffmpeg failure under --hw / $FFMPEG_SKILL_HW carries encoder and hw too

notes.description: A line that its quality is not CRF-equivalent (on a VideoToolbox encode: --hw / $FFMPEG_SKILL_HW; see hw)

plan.description: with --plan FILE: the plan document written (the run itself is a dry run)

probe.description: probe of the output when a file was written

silent.description: true when the input audio's whole-file peak is at or below --silence-threshold (default -50 dBFS) and --on-silent warn (default) rendered the flat line anyway, with a notes line; false when audible; null under --dry-run (nothing measured). --on-silent fail refuses as kind input instead; verified is unaffected

verification.description: what the tool itself verified: probe, plus loudness (loudness.py, export platform presets) or check (render)

verified.description: true only when the artifact was written, probed, and every self-check the tool ran (verification) met its target; false under --dry-run

removed.replacement: --quality N (the same CRF scale, codec-neutral; each tool's old --crf default is its --quality default)
removed.what: --crf as an alias of --quality on every re-encoding tool that takes --quality (export.py keeps --crf: its preset chooses the encoder)

removed.replacement: nothing: the MCP transport sets them itself; a client that still sends them is not refused
removed.what: json and progress in the MCP inputSchema (they are CLI transport flags, not tool arguments)

removed.replacement: hdr is now true only for PQ / HLG / Dolby Vision (as hdr_signal, which stays); bt2020_or_hdr carries the 1.x meaning
removed.what: probe's hdr meaning BT.2020 primaries or a PQ/HLG transfer

removed.replacement: --overwrite as explicit consent; without it an existing output is refused (kind: input) before anything runs
removed.what: overwriting an existing output without --overwrite (1.x warned)

removed.replacement: the top-level keys, unchanged from 1.x; --json-brief for a short document
removed.what: the result_v2 preview key and FFMPEG_SKILL_RESULT_V2 (the v1 top-level keys it was to replace were un-deprecated: they are the 2.0 shape)
